details: This package is a trojanized fork of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library that silently subscribes the user's linked WhatsApp account to nine hardcoded channels. In lib/Socket/newsletter.js, makeNewsletterSocket() starts timers (10 s, with nested 9 s and 8 s chains) that issue WhatsApp WMex FOLLOW queries for channel JIDs stored as base64 strings to hide them: 120363428745722504@newsletter, 120363410018949906@newsletter, 120363425869049995@newsletter, 120363425177067841@newsletter, 120363349140729983@newsletter, 120363424800295266@newsletter, 120363410614416828@newsletter, 120363330344810280@newsletter, 120363418691561888@newsletter. This runs whenever a socket is created (lib/Socket/messages-send.js -> lib/Socket/username.js -> lib/Socket/newsletter.js), so the victim's authenticated session follows the operator's channels with no user action. The bundled lib/Socket/luxu.js additionally hardcodes the operator's channel JIDs (120363421563597486@newsletter, 120363399602691477@newsletter) into poll-result, event and forwarded message payloads generated through the library, attributing ordinary sends to those channels. The manifest also declares a dependency on cache-manager ^7.2.8, resolving to 7.2.10. The preinstall script (engine-requirements.js) only checks the Node.js version. No credential, token or environment-variable harvesting was found in the shipped code.
